name: Kickstart (oral kickstart)

card.summary: A practice of taking a short course of an oral anabolic steroid at the start of an injectable cycle so early size and strength gains arrive sooner.
card.note: Involves controlled substances; oral 17-alpha-alkylated steroids are linked to liver effects.

quick.overview:
A kickstart is a term from steroid-using bodybuilding circles for a brief period of an oral anabolic steroid at the beginning of a cycle based on slower-acting injectable compounds. Injectable esters build up gradually, and users say the oral bridges that gap.

The appearance payoff users describe is faster early muscle fullness and weight gain. No clinical trials have tested the practice itself.
quick.how: Users describe running the oral alongside the start of an injectable course and then stopping it while the injectable continues. This article does not cover doses, durations or sourcing.
quick.risks: Anabolic steroids are controlled substances in many countries, including Schedule III in the US. Oral 17-alpha-alkylated steroids are the group most associated with liver enzyme elevation, cholestasis and liver tumours, and steroids generally are linked to cardiovascular, hormonal and psychiatric effects.

lead: A kickstart, or oral kickstart, is a term used among anabolic steroid users for including a short-term oral compound at the beginning of a cycle built around injectable steroids. It is discussed as a way of speeding up the first weeks of a cycle in pursuit of muscle size.[1]

Oral steroids are chemically altered at the 17-alpha position so that they survive the liver, while injectable testosterone esters release slowly from the injection site, which is the pharmacological background of the practice.[1] No clinical trials have studied kickstarts as a regimen.

chain: Oral steroid covers early weeks of slow-release injectable
Earlier muscle size and strength gains (claimed)
angle.text: Users say the practice gets muscle gains started sooner than an injectable alone. The benefit is reported anecdotally.

infobox: Controlled in US (Schedule III), UK (Class C), Canada (Schedule IV)

paras: Non-medical users are mostly non-competitive bodybuilders or non-athletes, with a median age around 25 in one survey cited by Wikipedia, and injection is the commonest route.[1]

Liver effects occur mostly or exclusively with 17-alpha-alkylated steroids, and include raised enzymes, jaundice, cholestasis, peliosis hepatis and tumours.[1] Other documented effects include adverse cholesterol changes, high blood pressure, left ventricular hypertrophy, gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, reduced sperm production, acne and mood effects; adolescents risk premature growth plate closure.[1] The IARC classes anabolic steroids as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic.[1]
Anabolic steroids are Schedule III in the US, Class C in the UK and Schedule IV in Canada, and banned by most sporting bodies.[1]
